scenes.script_line: Your story has shifted. What happens next is how you begin to live from it. For some people, this happens naturally. For others, a simple structure helps reinforce what has already changed. That's what step ten is for. Why measure at all? Because what we pay attention to grows. When you notice your progress, you strengthen it. And when you notice where you're slipping, you can respond early, before the old story settles back in. It's optional, but it can make a real difference to how consistent and lasting this work becomes.

scenes.script_line: On page twenty, you'll see three types of accountability. The first is self accountability. This is your personal commitment to live from what you've defined. A quiet awareness of how you think, speak and act, in line with your new story. The second is partner accountability. Someone you trust, who knows about the shift you've made. They support you by reflecting back what they see, and reinforcing the direction you're moving in.

shots.text: person writing a quiet personal note to themselves
two people talking, one checking in warmly with the other
close-up of two hands exchanging a written note

scenes.script_line: The third is tribe accountability. A group where growth is shared. Being around others who are also living from what's true creates momentum and encouragement. When choosing a partner, look for someone who will be honest and kind. Not someone who will simply agree with you, and not someone who will judge you. A simple check-in, once a week, can be enough. What did I do that fits my new story? Where did the old story show up? What will I do next?

shots.text: small group sitting together, sharing progress openly
person listening closely to a trusted peer, honest expression
close-up of a hand writing three short check-in questions

scenes.script_line: You might choose one, or all three. Write down which ones you'll use, and who will be involved. Be specific here too. Not "I'll find someone," but a name, and a time you'll check in. You can also create a simple daily alignment practice. Reading your new story. Reflecting on it for a moment. Or taking one small action that fits it. Not as a rule, but as a way of reinforcing what is already true.

shots.text: person writing a specific name and day in a planner
close-up of a hand circling a date on a calendar
shots.pexels: hand circling date calendar close up

shots.text: person reading their new story quietly each morning

scenes.script_line: Over time, you'll notice progress in a simple way. What you believe, what you say, and how you live begin to move together. And if you slip, that's normal. Progress is rarely a straight line. What matters is that you notice, and return. Your facilitator will help you choose your accountability and set it up before you leave.
